text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: sustained KV cache growth detected on cluster-east-1 > paging events increasing 3x, p99 latency rising. Auto-escalation -> incidents channel.

leo_oncall: I'm on it. confirming spike seen in dashboards (kv_bytes and eviction_rate).

alice_sre: thx leo. any customer impact yet?

maya_prod-support: getting a report from Sam (enterprise customer) about ~3-5s tail latency on chat endpoints.

sam_customer: seeing timeouts on long-context prompts, we had two sessions drop. happy to share logs if helpful.

leo_oncall: can someone pull a top-20 heavy models list for the last 30m? suspect recent AWQ/int8 rollout routing change.

dmitry_runtime: pulling now. initial quick check: model-id rwd-awq-lr-2 recently added to the quantized-kernel routing pool ~40 mins ago. it's responsible for ~28% of kv growth.

katie_ml: interesting — AWQ kernel change included a new kv-serialization tweak to store int8 keys with expanded dtype for alignment. noticed small size bump in bench but not this much.

alice_sre: action plan drafts: (1) remove rwd-awq-lr-2 from quant routing -> route to fp16 kernel fallback, (2) reduce continuous batching window for affected nodes, (3) enable IGNOREFORCE prefix-eviction for that model, (4) initiate rolling worker restart if eviction doesn't reduce memory.

leo_oncall: doing step 1 now.

# command
```
# admin-api patch to routing pool
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routing/remove \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-awq-lr-2","pool":"quantized-kernels"}'
```

dmitry_runtime: removed model from quantized pool, re-routing to fp16. verifying kernel selection on a few machines.

# logs from worker-23 after re-route
```
2026-03-15T14:21:10Z INFO kernel_select: selected=fp16_optimized for model=rwd-awq-lr-2 node=worker-23
2026-03-15T14:21:11Z WARN kv_cache: evicted=1223 entries, freed=4.8GB
```

leo_oncall: eviction freed ~5GB on that node. overall cluster eviction rate down by ~60% in 6m. latency p99 improved but still above baseline for some customers.

maya_prod-support: Sam — can you confirm if tail latency improved?

sam_customer: latency dropped for most calls. still occasional 2.5s spikes on long contexts, but no more timeouts. thanks.

katie_ml: follow-up: the AWQ kernel change doubled per-kv metadata from 16->32 bytes due to alignment padding on certain transformer shapes; combined with int8 packing this amplifies worst-case contexts. the regression wasn't visible in microbench because typical ctx lengths were lower.

alice_sre: we need a hotfix to prevent recurrence until kernel patch lands: (A) add config guard to quant-routing that enforces per-model kv_limit_bytes, (B) enforce max_continuous_batch_tokens=256 on quant pool, (C) add early fallback rule when kv_size_ratio > 1.5x baseline.

leo_oncall: applying hotfix to cluster config now. patch below.

```
# patch snippet
- pool: quantized-kernels
  config:
+   kv_limit_bytes: 4GB
+   max_continuous_batch_tokens: 256
+   fallback_on_kv_ratio: 1.5
```

# api call
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/pools/patch -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d @patch.yml

leo_oncall: patch applied to cluster-east-1 and canary nodes.

tomas_infra: started rolling restarts on 10% of affected workers to clear stale KV metadata and force new kernel selection logic.

dmitry_runtime: observed a secondary issue: when fp16 fallback selected, some RPC serialization paths hit an unexpected code path causing slightly higher CPU on host; watching for regressions.

alice_sre: note that CPU bump is acceptable short-term vs paging. notify infra if CPU spike threatens other tenants.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation step recorded: removed rwd-awq-lr-2 from quant pool; pool-level limits applied; rolling restarts initiated. No longer paging at scale.

maya_prod-support: updating affected customers. Sam — are you able to run a few regression prompts for us in the next 30m?

sam_customer: yes, sending a couple of examples via DM now.

katie_ml: immediate engineering action items (short):
- revert AWQ alignment padding in kernel (katie/Dmitry)
- add kv_size synthetic tests to CI for long-context prompts (katie)
- add a model-level kv_size alarm with auto-fallback (dmitry)

alice_sre: ops todo (short):
- bake kv_limit_bytes into pool defaults (alice)
- add runbook step to emergency-route models to dedicated capacity (leo)
- add customer-facing sysmsg template for latency incidents (maya)

dmitry_runtime: also adding an opt-in telemetry tag so we can measure per-model kv_bytes by quantization path (awq/gptq/int8). will push in next deploy.

leo_oncall: status update: last_message_ts=1912345989. cluster back to steady eviction rates, p99 latency within 1.2x baseline. marking incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: :mag_right: Postmortem checklist created and assigned: katie_ml (root cause analysis), dmitry_runtime (kernel rollback), alice_sre (runbook updates), maya_prod-support (customer comms).

maya_prod-support: I drafted customer email for impacted enterprise tenants. will share for review.

sam_customer: appreciate the quick triage. please keep me posted once kernel patch is out.

alice_sre: agreed. once kernel fix lands we'll remove the temporary kv_limit and bump back pooling settings after controlled canary.

katie_ml: root cause summary (short): AWQ kernel alignment change increased per-kv metadata for long contexts; combined with continuous batching behavior and a model that produced long prefixes caused exponential KV growth -> paging. Fix: revert alignment, add kv-size CI, add pool-level kv limits and auto-fallback.

leo_oncall: thanks team. incident closed for now, will track follow-ups in the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
